messages:
rachel: Heads up — noticed p95 and p99 numbers diverge weirdly when I filter the latency dashboard by endpoint vs by route. p95 looks fine, but p99 jumps ~40% for /v1/generate only when endpoint filter is applied. anyone seen this?

samir: hmm. do you have the raw counts? could be sampling difference between the rollup path and the endpoint slice.

rachel: yeah attaching the quick query I ran. short version: when I compare route="/generate" (rollup) vs endpoint="/generate-us-east-1" (endpoint) the sample counts differ a lot. p99 delta persists after normalizing per-sample.

rachel: ```sql
SELECT percentile_cont(0.99) AS p99, count(*) AS n
FROM latency_events
WHERE route = '/generate' AND ts > now() - interval '1h'
```

hema: are we using t-digest rollups for route-level aggregates? could be compression artifacts if the route digest is merging very different endpoint distributions.

rachel: yes route rollups use tdigest with compression=200. endpoint metrics are raw histograms (no tdigest merge).

andrew: that matches a common cause — tdigest merge can under/overestimate extreme quantiles when distributions are multi-modal. endpoints might have a long tail from a single AZ that gets diluted in the rollup.

anya: also check sampling: dashboard queries default to 1% sampling on high-cardinality views. endpoint filter might disable sampling (or hit a different code path) so n changes.

rachel: good call. dashboard query options: sampling=auto. when I force sampling=0 both views line up more closely but still ~10% gap.

samir: can you paste the console query that the UI issues? there was a subtle difference — UI used `quantile(0.99, latency)` vs backend `tdigest.quantile(0.99)` depending on aggregation path.

rachel: here: UI logs show: `/api/metrics?group_by=route&quantile=0.99&merge=tdigest&sampling=auto`. for endpoint: `/api/metrics?group_by=endpoint&quantile=0.99&histogram=true&sampling=off`.

hema: ok that's our smoking gun — two different codepaths. one merges tdigest rollups, the other computes against histogram buckets. they have different biases at the tail.

andrew: long term we should unify to a single contract for percentile queries (either return tdigest-derived quantiles for everything or force histogram-quantiles everywhere). short term we can add a dashboard hint: "Compare like-for-like aggregation mode".

anya: UX idea: add a small badge on the chart that shows "aggregation=tdigest" or "aggregation=histogram" so users don't get confused.

rachel: agree. also worth adding a note in the tooltip: sample count + aggregation method.

infra-bot: deploy 2498765800: rolling out dashboard-telemetry-legend (adds aggregation hint) to staging.

samir: for the correctness part we should run a quick experiment: pick a handful of endpoints, export raw latencies, compute p50/p95/p99 by direct sort, compare to tdigest and histogram outputs. if tdigest error > threshold we need to adjust compression or switch algorithm.

hema: I'm happy to run that. threshold proposal: abs(tdigest_p99 - true_p99) / true_p99 > 0.05 => alert (5%).

rachel: thanks. can you also check if routing policy (like fallback routing to cheaper region) changes the per-request tags so they end up in different endpoint buckets? that could cause jumps too.

hema: good point — I'll cross-check routing logs for any surprising route rewrites in the last hour.

andrew: FYI, for Dedicated customers we already expose raw per-host histograms (no tdigest). maybe the quick fix is to surface a toggle: "use raw histograms for percentiles" in the console. low-risk UX change.

anya: +1 on toggle. but we should default to the cheaper/fast path (tdigest) and warn when the two disagree.

rachel: next steps: 1) hema runs the ground-truth comparison and routing log check; 2) samir files a tiny backend PR to add aggregation method into the UI payload; 3) anya wires a badge/tooltip in staging; 4) andrew drafts a short doc note on what aggregation to use for accuracy vs cost tradeoff. I'll file tasks.

samir: thanks — ping me once you have numbers, I can run a quick sensitivity test on compression param.

infra-bot: note: created ticket INF-2142 "dashboard: surface aggregation method and sample count" assigned to samir/anya; ETA 3d.

rachel: awesome. marking as follow-up in the dashboard board. :spiral_calendar: 

hema: starting experiment now, will post results in this thread.

rachel: thanks team :heart:
